data.summary: 13/13 backlog tasks are genuinely implemented in the merged tree (verified file-by-file against the diff, not against reports). A forced --rerun-tasks per-module desktop run executed 191 tests across 7 test-bearing modules with 0 failures and 0 skips. No AC is unimplemented. Four ACs (AC-5, AC-7, AC-9, AC-51) cannot be closed by any artefact in this repo and need a human demo/render pass; that is an environment limit already recorded, not a defect. Two substantive behavioural findings are raised for a human ruling (AF-1 popover visibility asymmetry, AF-2 SC-4 demo is unreachable without pressing Escape first). Scope discipline is clean.

findings.issue: Popover visibility is asymmetric between the crowded and uncrowded cases, and the uncrowded case loses information. SelectedComment renders a popover for the SELECTED annotation only (`val selected = frozen.selected ?: return`). AnnotationGutter — which renders a read-only AnnotationPopover for every NON-selected annotation — is composed only when `anyOverlap(...)` is true. Net effect: with two uncrowded annotations, the comment typed on #1 disappears from the stage the moment #2 is selected (it survives only in the Notes side panel); with two CROWDED annotations the same comment stays visible in the gutter. Crowding therefore makes more content appear, not less. FR-8 reads 'show a per-annotation popover'; the implementation shows one editable popover plus, conditionally, read-only copies.
findings.evidence: presentation-feature-mirror/src/commonMain/kotlin/presentation/feature/mirror/source/mirror/MirrorAnnotationStage.kt:273-286 (`if (anyOverlap(nominalPopoverRects(...))) { AnnotationGutter(...) }` then unconditional `SelectedComment(...)`) and :478 (`val selected = frozen.selected ?: return`). No test covers it; no preview shows the uncrowded-two-annotation case (MirrorFrozenStagePreview has selectedIndex = 2 and its two marks are far apart, so it renders exactly this state with annotation #1's comment invisible).
findings.description: Non-selected annotations show no popover unless crowding triggers the gutter, so committed comments vanish from the stage in the uncrowded case while staying visible in the crowded one.

findings.issue: SC-4's canonical state ('draw three annotation boxes close together, popovers relocate to the gutter') is not reachable by performing SC-4's own steps. `stageAnnotation` auto-selects every new annotation (`selectedIndex = staged.size`) and `AnnotationGutter` excludes the selected one (`filter { it.index != frozen.selectedIndex }`), so after the third drag the gutter holds 2 rows, never 3. The operator must press Escape before the state the scenario describes exists. T-11's own report flags this, so it is known — but it means the SC-4/AC-9 demo screenshot cannot be shot by following the scenario verbatim, and the scenario text should be amended rather than the behaviour quietly diverging from it.

findings.issue: B3's hit-test reasoning is SOUND and the fix is correct. Verified: (a) detectDragGestures begins with awaitFirstDown(requireUnconsumed = false), so consumption by a descendant genuinely cannot stop it — only failing to be hit can; (b) Compose hit-tests a Box's children back-to-front and stops descending into lower siblings once one reports a hit, and the drag layer is an EARLIER sibling than SelectedComment and the Resume Live button, so the popover plate and the button take the pointer; (c) the shield is on an ANCESTOR of the text field, and ancestors do not remove descendants from the hit path — the field keeps its own click, caret placement and selection-drag gestures, which are unmodified kit code. One nit: the shield's `awaitEachGesture { awaitFirstDown(...) }` body is ceremonial — a pointerInput node participates in hit testing regardless of what its handler does, so `pointerInput(Unit) {}` would shield identically. Harmless; keep or simplify.
findings.evidence: MirrorAnnotationStage.kt:226-296 (sibling ordering) and :532-536 (popoverPointerShield); CommentPopover.kt CommentField is an unmodified BasicTextField under that Box.
findings.description: B3's hit-test fix verified sound; shield's suspend body is ceremonial but harmless.

findings.issue: RULING on the hand-written FakeFrameBitmap: the test is a REAL assertion, not circular. The fake supplies only identity plus two deliberately distinct dimensions (width = 100 + bytes.size, height = 200 + 2*bytes.size); it has no knowledge of and no influence over WHICH instance the ViewModel pins, which is the entirety of AC-47. The load-bearing assertion is `assertSame(atRelease, viewModel.frozenFrame.value)` — object identity, which a fake cannot fake. Two independent strengtheners: (1) both axes differ per frame, so a one-dimension coincidence cannot pass it; (2) the asserted deviceSize (109x218) is deliberately unequal to MirrorFrameModel.widthPx/heightPx (1080x2400, constant across both frames), which proves FrozenFrame.deviceSize is derived from the pinned BITMAP rather than from the frame model — a stronger claim than the AC asked for. Residual limit, correctly bounded: readPixels is a no-op, so the test asserts which bitmap object was pinned, never which pixels. Since the ViewModel only ever stores a reference, that is exactly the right scope. The companion test `secondDragAddsAnnotationWithoutRefreezing` covers the opposite direction (a newer frame must NOT displace the pinned one). Implementing the ImageBitmap interface by hand was the correct call over adding a Skiko dependency or a build.gradle.kts edit.

findings.description: AC-47's hand-rolled ImageBitmap fake is sound — assertSame on identity cannot be satisfied circularly.

findings.issue: CONFIRMED from the real diff: freezing is render-only and Resume Live costs no reconnection. MirrorViewModel.kt's diff has exactly five hunks (@@ -1, -82, -103, -169, -225); `sessionDeviceId` appears in only two of them, both pre-existing lines inside selectPlatform/stopSession that already set it to null, and the flatMapLatest capture gate / observeFrames region is not in any hunk at all — byte-identical. stageAnnotation and resumeLive touch only currentFrozenFrame and the reducer. The test evidence matches the code: resumeLiveClearsTheFrozenFrameAndAnnotations asserts session == Streaming(PHONE), startedDevices == [PHONE] and activeCollectors == 1 after Resume Live, i.e. the collector was never torn down.

aggregateDiffFindings.issue: Popover visibility asymmetry between the crowded and uncrowded cases (AF-1), and gutter popovers are unshielded against the drag layer while the selected popover is shielded (AF-6). Both sit on the T-7/T-11 seam, which is why neither task caught it.

Drag state is read in the composable body, so each pointer move recomposes the stage subtree including the frame Image rather than invalidating draw only (AF-7). Does not affect NFR-1's capture/transport budget.

No security surface touched. No file I/O, no serialization, no network, no new dependency, no reflection, no logging of frame bytes. The frozen bitmap is a second in-memory reference released on Resume Live, platform switch and session stop (MirrorViewModel.kt resumeLive/selectPlatform/stopSession all null currentFrozenFrame), so a pinned frame cannot outlive the session that produced it. Annotation text never leaves memory (export is F-7).

popoverPointerShield's awaitEachGesture body does no work that hit-testing does not already do (AF-5). Also: a duplicated ShowDivider() and two out-of-order imports in StyleguideScreen.kt (AF-9). Nothing unreachable; no orphaned declarations — every new internal (FrameGeometry, MIN_DRAG_DEVICE_PX, metaLine, sizeLabel, anyOverlap, closesPopover, NOMINAL_POPOVER_*) has both a production call site and a test.

The toolbar's 'Clear' / 'staged' / 'Resolve & Send' strings remain hardcoded English in a file this spec edited. Pre-existing and consistent with that file (zero stringResource calls in RectifyWindow.kt, by its own convention of driving the shell from literals), so T-12 correctly left them alone — recorded only so a later i18n pass over compose-application knows where to start.

Notes auto-selection keys on `stagedCount >= 1`, so after Clear Staged drops the count to 0 the next annotation re-selects the Notes tab. Matches the recorded intent ('the first annotation of a frozen frame only') on any reasonable reading, and the user explicitly asked for Clear in that case. Noted, not faulted.
